title: Depressive symptoms among adult patients with systemic lupus erythematosus in the Jazan Region, Saudi Arabia: An analytical cross-sectional study
content:
by Aliyah Mansour Alhamoud, Siham Elamin Habeeballah

Mental disorders, including depression, are common among patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). Depressive symptoms can significantly impair quality of life and are associated with adverse clinical outcomes. Studies investigating depressive symptoms and their associated factors in individuals with SLE have yielded inconsistent findings. Therefore, this study aimed to determine the prevalence of depressive symptoms among patients with SLE and to identify the associated factors in patients from the Jazan Region of Saudi Arabia. An analytical cross-sectional study of 112 patients with SLE in Jazan, Saudi Arabia was conducted in 2023. A convenience sampling technique was used to recruit all eligible adult patients with SLE who attended rheumatology clinics and day-care units at the referral hospitals in the region. Depressive symptoms were assessed using the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9). Chi-square tests and binary logistic regression analyses were used to examine associations and identify factors associated with depressive symptoms. The majority of participants were female (104 [92.9%]), with ages ranging from 18 to 59 years. Depressive symptoms were present in 80% of participants, with patients experiencing mild depression 25 (22%), moderate depression 28 (25%), moderate-to-severe depression 22 (20%), and severe depression 15 (13%).In the multivariable analysis, although physical activity as a categorical variable did not reach overall statistical significance (global p = 0.067), participants engaging in less than 150 minutes of physical activity per week were significantly less likely to experience depressive symptoms compared with those performing no physical activity (OR = 0.28; 95% CI 0.10–0.82; P = 0.020).In conclusion, depressive symptoms were highly prevalent among patients with SLE in the Jazan Region, and physical activity level was identified as a significant modifiable associated factor in this population. Routine screening could facilitate early detection and intervention in patients with SLE in similar settings, resulting in improved clinical outcomes.
